stories.headline: Colorado faces $1.6 billion budget deficit as Medicaid costs surge out of control
stories.summary:
Colorado budget analysts delivered grim news to the Joint Budget Committee on Friday, projecting a $1.6 billion deficit for the 2027-28 fiscal year — far worse than the best-case scenario economists had offered just three months ago. The collapse of the June forecast was driven almost entirely by runaway Medicaid spending, which the state's budget director called an existential risk to all other state services.

The state overspent its healthcare budget by $213 million in the fiscal year that ended June 30, and the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing projects an additional $443 million bust in the current budget, plus $918 million in added costs the following year. Despite Medicaid enrollment falling 31% since 2023, costs have risen 92% over the same period, driven by surging use of long-term care services for the elderly and behavioral health treatment.

Federal policy changes under the Trump administration are compounding the problem. Starting in 2027-28, Colorado expects to lose $105 million annually from a new federal cap on state hospital provider fees used to help fund Medicaid, with deeper restrictions phased in over time. Mark Ferrandino, director of the governor's Office of State Planning and Budgeting, warned that if Medicaid spending continues growing at its current 13.6% annual rate, it will crowd out all other state departments by the end of the next decade.

The dire projections arrive ahead of a November election featuring multiple ballot measures that could affect the state's fiscal picture. The findings will set the stage for painful spending cut decisions by the state legislature and Colorado's next governor.

stories.headline: KSE announces $135 million renovation of Ball Arena, with construction set to begin in 2027
stories.summary:
Kroenke Sports & Entertainment announced Friday a $135 million privately funded renovation of Ball Arena, the 27-year-old downtown Denver venue that is home to the Nuggets, Avalanche and Mammoth. The project centers on a 30,000-square-foot expansion of the arena's east lobby, enclosed by a new glass facade, with escalators, an enlarged team store, and an increase in east entrance doors from eight to 20.

Additional upgrades include widened concourses and ingress and egress points in high-traffic areas, three new premium clubs — including one with direct access to reserved 100-level seating — and technology improvements aimed at reducing wait times. A large outdoor LED screen and a 34,000-square-foot pedestrian plaza facing Chopper Circle are also part of the plans. A required site development plan was submitted to the City of Denver on Friday.

Construction is scheduled to begin in summer 2027 and conclude in fall 2028, carried out in phases to minimize disruption to fans and neighbors. The renovations follow previously announced upgrades to Ball Arena's luxury suites, which are expected to debut during the upcoming 2026-27 season.

KSE chairman E. Stanley Kroenke said the project is part of a commitment to keep Denver's sports teams competitive for another 25 years. The announcement also signals a delay in the broader River Mile redevelopment along the South Platte River, as KSE's near-term focus shifts to Ball Arena and surrounding property near Speer Boulevard.

stories.headline: Children's Hospital Colorado placed on lockdown after swatting call, all patients and staff safe
stories.summary:
Children's Hospital Colorado in Aurora was temporarily locked down Friday morning after a caller reported a possible shooting inside the facility. Aurora Police Department officers responded to the hospital at 13100 East 16th Avenue just before 8:20 a.m. and quickly determined the report was a swatting call — a false emergency designed to trigger a large law enforcement response.

Officers swept the building and secured it by approximately 10:30 a.m. All patients and staff were reported safe. A police spokesperson said the call originated from a phone number with a documented history of making similar false emergency calls to other locations.

Because the call came from a voice line, investigators said it is difficult to immediately identify the person responsible. Aurora police said they are working with federal partners on a follow-up investigation.

stories.headline: Second measles case this week adds Union Station, Steamboat Springs hotel to Colorado exposure list
stories.summary:
A second measles case in as many days has been confirmed in Colorado, with state health officials identifying Denver's Union Station and a Steamboat Springs hotel as potential exposure sites. The infected individual, a visitor to Colorado, may have exposed others at Union Station on Tuesday evening between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m., and at the La Quinta Inn in Steamboat Springs on Wednesday between 9 a.m. and 2:30 p.m.

The case follows a separate confirmed measles infection announced Tuesday, in which another visitor spent time at the Pearl Street Mall in Boulder and a hotel in Westminster. Colorado had recorded 25 measles cases as of Sept. 15 this year, with 22 of those cases occurring in unvaccinated individuals and 19 involving children and teens under 18.

State health officials warn that people who were present at the identified locations may develop symptoms — including fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes and a facial rash — through Oct. 7. Anyone experiencing symptoms is urged to call their healthcare provider before visiting a clinic and to contact the state public health department at 720-653-3369.

Colorado's 25 confirmed cases this year are slightly lower than the 31 recorded at the same point in 2025, though the new cases have not yet been added to the state's official count. An updated list of all exposure locations statewide is available through the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment.

stories.headline: Colorado private jet company OneFlight pauses all flights, raising concerns over $150 million in prepaid customer funds
stories.summary:
One Flight International, a charter jet broker operating out of Centennial Airport in Englewood, has suspended all flight operations for at least 30 days while conducting what it described as a comprehensive review of its operations. The company deleted its Facebook and Instagram accounts and has not responded to phone inquiries, raising alarm among customers and aviation industry observers.

Private aviation analyst Doug Gollan, editor of Private Jet Card Comparisons, said customers had prepaid more than $150 million for future flights through the company's jet card program, and warned those funds could go unused. Gollan first raised concerns in a Forbes article about the sudden operational pause.

Adding to questions about the company's stability, its chief financial officer, Johannes Uys, is in immigration detention in Aurora after being arrested in July on domestic violence-related charges. It is unclear when Uys was detained or whether he was still active with the company at the time. Chief operating executive Ferren Rajput could not be reached for comment.

The company's website states it is evaluating its current operations and status. The situation remains fluid, and the extent of financial exposure for customers holding prepaid jet card balances has not been independently confirmed.

stories.headline: Colorado Supreme Court halts mandatory courtroom livestreaming, citing harassment and threats to fair trials
stories.summary:
Colorado Supreme Court Chief Justice Monica Márquez issued a directive Tuesday pausing the mandatory livestreaming of courtroom proceedings for the next three months, allowing individual judges to decide on a case-by-case basis whether to broadcast hearings. The move puts the court's directive in direct conflict with a 2023 state law requiring all criminal proceedings to be livestreamed by default.

Márquez cited a surge of reports from across the state's court system describing how livestream footage has been illegally recorded and uploaded to YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and Facebook — often by accounts that monetize the content through advertising revenue. She wrote that the technology intended to broaden public access to courts had been "subverted as a tool of disruption, disparagement, harassment, and private economic gain."

The concerns are not merely procedural. In one case, a livestream of a sexual assault trial was posted to YouTube with the victim's identifying information visible. In another high-profile case in 2025, an attorney for Barry Morphew argued that popular YouTube accounts with hundreds of thousands of subscribers were livestreaming proceedings, generating viewer commentary that included threats against the judge, attorneys and victims.

All chief judges in Colorado's judicial districts supported the pause, according to a spokesperson for the judicial department. The three-month period is intended to give the court time to develop a more durable policy framework. In-person attendance at hearings and virtual participation for case parties will not be affected.

stories.headline: St. Mary's Glacier disappears for first time in recorded history after historic drought and heat
stories.summary:
St. Mary's Glacier, a semi-permanent snowfield near Idaho Springs that has attracted year-round skiers and hikers for well over a century, has melted away entirely for what is believed to be the first time in recorded history. The disappearance follows a winter season that set consecutive daily lows in snowpack and a summer that was Colorado's hottest on record with 132 years of data.

Snowpack in the South Platte River Basin peaked at just 8.5 inches of snow water equivalent on March 17 — well below the normal 16.1-inch peak — and was declared non-existent by June 6, eleven days ahead of schedule. Daily low snowpack records were broken every day from March 21 through May 4. Clear Creek County, where the snowfield is located, has been in Stage 2 drought or worse since February 2026.

Climate scientists say the disappearance is part of a broader trend. Colorado is home to more than 135 permanent snow or ice bodies, but only 14 qualify as true glaciers. An adjunct professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver's Earth and Atmospheric Sciences Department warned that the state could lose all of its named glaciers by 2080, with implications for water supply and recreation.

Experts say St. Mary's Glacier should reform if Colorado receives adequate snowfall this winter, but note that the event signals increasing vulnerability for the state's remaining ice features. The snowfield has been documented as a recreational destination since at least 1902 and was the site of a ski resort that operated from the 1930s to 1986.

stories.headline: Aspen Acres Fire victims denied federal individual disaster assistance, state says
stories.summary:
Victims of the Aspen Acres Fire and subsequent flooding in Colorado will not receive individual assistance from the federal government for disaster recovery, according to an announcement from Denver7. The denial means affected residents will not have access to direct federal aid programs that can cover temporary housing, home repairs and other personal losses.

The decision is a significant setback for families displaced or damaged by the fire and related flooding events. Without federal individual assistance, survivors must rely on state programs, local aid organizations and private insurance to rebuild and recover.

stories.headline: Broncos return to basics ahead of Week 2 home game against Jacksonville after record-setting defensive collapse
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos are focusing on fundamental tackling and assignment discipline this week after a historically poor defensive performance in their season-opening loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Denver's 29.8% missed tackle rate was the third-worst recorded in an NFL game since 2018, and the Broncos allowed 247 missed-tackle yards — the most by any defense in that same span, according to Next Gen Stats.

Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph characterized the fixes as straightforward and expressed confidence that the team would perform better when it hosts the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2 at Empower Field. The Jaguars are 1-0 on the season and were the only team to beat Denver at home during the 2025 regular season.

Head coach Sean Payton also publicly backed offensive coordinator Davis Webb following a rough debut as the team's play-caller in the Monday Night Football loss. The Broncos and Jaguars kick off Sunday.

stories.headline: Nuggets sign former Rockets first-round pick Cam Whitmore to two-way contract ahead of training camp
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets have signed 22-year-old wing Cam Whitmore to a two-way contract, filling their last available spot of that type on the roster, according to two league sources confirmed by The Denver Post. Whitmore was the 20th overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft by Houston but never secured a consistent role with the Rockets or, more recently, the Washington Wizards.

Whitmore arrived in Denver as a bookkeeping piece in the five-team Peyton Watson sign-and-trade completed in August. The Cleveland Cavaliers, who briefly held his rights, waived and stretched his contract, leaving them responsible for $1.8 million in dead cap space over three years. The Nuggets were then able to sign him for a $0 cap hit.

Despite his two-way designation, Whitmore is considered an unusually high-upside addition. He has averaged 10.5 points and 3.3 rebounds per game in 17.3 minutes across his first three NBA seasons, and converted 54% of his two-point attempts last year — a career best. He has already begun informal workouts with the team ahead of training camp.

With the signing, Denver now carries three two-way players: Whitmore, KJ Simpson and rookie Bryce Hopkins. The team has one standard roster spot remaining and currently holds two 2023 first-round picks, with Whitmore joining Julian Strawther.

stories.headline: GRiZ announces two free Denver concerts after fans locked out of sold-out Red Rocks shows
stories.summary:
Electronic artist GRiZ, also known as Grant Kwiecinski, announced Thursday that he will perform two free concerts at Denver's Junkyard venue on Sunday, Sept. 27, in response to the overwhelming demand that left thousands of fans unable to obtain tickets to his sold-out Red Rocks Amphitheatre shows earlier this month. The Michigan-based artist cited the difficulty fans faced securing tickets as the motivation for the unusual move.

The free shows — set for 1 p.m. and 7 p.m. at Junkyard, 2323 W. Mulberry Place — will be the largest free concerts GRiZ has ever organized. The venue holds approximately 10,000 to 12,000 people depending on layout, roughly equivalent to the capacity of a single Red Rocks show. GRiZ said all merchandise proceeds from the day will be donated to local Denver charities.

Ticket reservations opened Friday morning at 10 a.m. via a dedicated link, with passes being non-transferable to curb resale activity. GRiZ also said he plans to return to Denver next year with a larger venue to better accommodate demand, a notable implicit critique of Red Rocks' 9,500-person capacity despite its global reputation.

joke.joke: Talking about music is like dancing about architecture.

topStory.headline: Macron Warns of Intensifying Russian Hybrid Attacks, Orders Plan to Protect French Infrastructure
topStory.summary:
French President Emmanuel Macron declared Thursday that Russia has stepped up hybrid attacks against France and Europe in recent weeks, vowing the campaign would not go without a response. Speaking at a news conference at the Elysee Palace following meetings with party leaders on security matters, Macron announced he had ordered a plan to safeguard critical infrastructure and defense industry sites against the escalating threat.

Macron cited a Russian-blamed drone attack on Leipzig airport in Germany last month and warned that Moscow's intent is to intimidate European nations and undermine their support for Ukraine. 'The result will be the exact opposite,' Macron said. 'We are not intimidated because we know that our security today and tomorrow is at stake in Ukraine.'

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk added to the alarm on Thursday, telling Polish lawmakers that Russian plans include drone and missile strikes against countries supporting Ukraine, with Moscow prepared to claim any such strikes were accidental in order to divide NATO. The warnings come after a Russian drone struck a passenger train near the Ukraine-Poland border last Sunday, shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and senior European security officials had traveled along the same rail line. Ukraine reported all passengers were evacuated minutes before the strike hit the train's engine near Yahodyn.

Hybrid warfare encompasses non-military methods such as cyberattacks, sabotage, and disinformation campaigns, often carried out through proxies. Russia has consistently denied involvement in such operations despite mounting evidence. A series of suspicious fires at defense facilities across Europe, from Italy to Estonia, has prompted several affected nations to publicly blame Moscow.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has maintained that Russia has no plans to attack Europe, but Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov warned Thursday that any European military intervention in Ukraine would constitute a declaration of war and trigger a swift response. Russia also reiterated Friday that British military facilities in Ukraine used to strike Russian territory would be considered legitimate targets, reserving the right to take counter-measures.
